summary: Owner correction: comparative lists and reader reception should drive synthesis; academic articles remain supporting evidence. Consulted Chinese and French reader rankings, one Reddit selection with dissent, and a broad nonfiction list. No new history-target research assigned.
next: Rebalance nonfiction membership and opening order, complete history category UI build, and preserve checkpoint.

sources.title: The 100 best nonfiction books of all time: the full list
sources.author: Robert McCrum
sources.note: A broad English-language selection spanning science, memoir, history, criticism, travel and reference. Display sequence is reverse chronological, not merit ranking; poetry, drama and fictional exceptions must be filtered.
sources.location: Complete numbered list; 98 title/author rows extracted, 82 and 100 held separately.
candidates: London Labour and the London Poor
The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
sources.limits: One editor and an English-language scope; not a cross-country consensus. Source inclusion does not settle nonfiction classification.

targets.A: Broad nonfiction candidates for all-subject comparison.
targets.N: Corrects concentration on philosophy by supplying history, science, memoir, travel, culture and reference works.

sources.title: 豆瓣读书 Top 250
sources.note: Examined the first two pages (50 entries). A Chinese-language reader-rating algorithm puts Chinese and translated books together. Includes historical biography, sociology, travel memoir and art history as well as fiction. Edition and series identities need normalization.
sources.location: Top 250 pages start=0 and start=25, first 50 displayed entries; only these pages consulted.
candidates: Deng Xiaoping and the Transformation of China
sources.limits: Platform users are not representative of all Chinese readers. Ratings depend on edition, number of ratings and algorithm; series and volumes are mixed. No full-250 consultation claimed.

targets.A: Independent Chinese-language reader reception and additional Chinese nonfiction candidates.
targets.L: Reader reception of prose fiction including Chinese works and translated classics; exclude nonfiction and unmatched series.
targets.N: Specific biography, social history, anthropology, travel and art-history works provide a reader counterweight to academic philosophy.

sources.title: My Top 50 Must Read Non-Fiction Books — list and reader objections
sources.author: Dependent-Bunch7505 and respondents
sources.note: The author explicitly calls the 50-item selection un-ordered and grouped by topic. It favors business and psychology; replies criticize narrowness and add women authors, history and biography, including Wilkerson and Skloot. Contains self-promotion, so use as one taste profile with dissent.
sources.location: Opening 50-item list and replies through the women-authors/history recommendations.
candidates: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
sources.limits: One personal selection, promotional context and self-selected comments; not a subreddit-wide ranking. Numbering is not merit rank.

targets.A: Reader preferences and disagreements across nonfiction subjects.
targets.N: Adds psychology, science, business, biography and social history while recording objections to an overly narrow selection.

sources.title: Le Top 111 livres — classement des membres
sources.note: The site describes a weekly ranking by member-average rating. Examined the first 20 entries, including fiction, Holocaust testimony, oral history and film interviews. French publication/volume identifiers differ from work-level English identities.
sources.limits: Member averages, not a representative French poll. Volume and translation effects are substantial; do not treat constituent-volume ranks as whole-series ranks.

targets.A: French-language reader reception outside the Anglophone institutional list tradition.
targets.L: Specific prose-fiction reception signals; preserve volume distinctions.
targets.N: Specific testimony, oral history and film-interview candidates, separately relevant to nonfiction.
